A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Efficient Adaptive Federated Optimization. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original federated-learning experiments on StackOverflow, CIFAR-100, and GLD-23K in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds FEMNIST and additional StackOverflow results in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: v1's FedAda2 becomes v2's FedAda2++, while the existing joint-adaptivity-without-preconditioner-communication procedure becomes FedAda2. Zero initialization, SM3 compression, server updates, delayed updates, and the detailed optimizer algorithms are retained.

E1.justification: v2 adds writer-partitioned FEMNIST for 62-class digit and letter recognition, extending image-domain coverage. StackOverflow, CIFAR-100, and GLD-23K remain.

E2.justification: The added StackOverflow comparison in v2 Figure 4 includes FedAdam alongside FedAdaGrad; v1's StackOverflow comparisons include only FedAdaGrad as the server-adaptive comparator. Other comparator families remain after matching renamed methods. MIME and MIMELite remain unevaluated resource comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds an Adam/one-local-epoch StackOverflow configuration alongside the retained AdaGrad/five-epoch configuration. FEMNIST introduces one- and five-epoch evaluations, client sampling settings, and a smaller hyperparameter grid. Existing DP parameters and retained hyperparameter selections remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 supplements the existing local-epoch analysis with FEMNIST comparisons at one and five epochs (Figure 7), and adds the StackOverflow optimizer/epoch variant (Figure 4). The heterogeneous-optimizer and delayed-update analyses remain in the appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 repetitions with different random seeds and shaded 95% confidence intervals. The added experiments use this existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands the reported results with FEMNIST learning curves and communication-cost comparisons, plus Adam/one-epoch StackOverflow results. It also replaces the appendix CIFAR-100 curves and reports SM3 second-moment storage at 0.48% of full storage for ViT. These changes do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4 adds bounded-server-iterate and lower-bounded-local-objective conditions. Appendix D.1 explicitly assumes clipping does not zero all gradients. The convergence rates and heavy-tailed-noise results are retained; moving the latter into Appendix A adds no new theorem.

C1.justification: v2 qualifies the originality of zero initialization by acknowledging its earlier appearance in reference [5]. It presents communication efficiency and memory reduction as separate variant contributions, while retaining the principal convergence and performance claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds an explanation of why positive smoothing parameters are necessary for the stated convergence bounds. v2 also corrects delayed updates' stated benefit from reducing communication to reducing client computation. The existing SM3 denoising hypothesis remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents FEMNIST's 500-client experimental subset, model/task specification, sampling, tuning grid, and selected hyperparameters in Figure 7, Tables 2, 5–6, and Appendix I.2. Existing preprocessing, hardware descriptions, and compute disclosure remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to LEAF, the MNIST/LeCun et al. paper, and Zhou et al. (2024). It newly acknowledges prior zero initialization in Wang et al. [5] and cites earlier evidence for client adaptivity. Broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: the former Section 3 becomes Appendix A, existing appendix proofs shift to Appendix B, the abstract and conclusion are rewritten, contributions become bullets, and variant terminology is recast throughout the main text.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 expand to four datasets, new multi-panel Figures 4 and 7 are added, and existing plots receive revised legends and axis ranges. A main-text resource table is added, appendix tables expand, and figures and algorithms are repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful validation, clearer memory accounting, and explicit theoretical restrictions. However, unlike v1's matching CIFAR-100 plots, v2 Figures 1 and 6 show different trajectories without a clear setting distinction. Several appendix descriptions and hyperparameter tables also retain conflicting older variant names. These unresolved consistency and reproducibility issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
